item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 090507
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Oct 8 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip
of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane Simon, located a
couple of hundred miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some gradual development of this system thereafter, and a
tropical depression could form as it moves generally
west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

&&

$$
Forecaster Evans/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 48
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 090244
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  48
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026
 
...RACHEL EXPECTED TO TURN NORTHEASTWARD LATER TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.6N 125.5W
ABOUT 995 MI...1600 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...990 MB...29.24 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in extreme northern Baja California, northern Gulf of 
California, and Southern California should monitor the progress of 
Rachel. Tropical Storm Watches could be required for a portion of 
this area later tonight.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 22.6 North, longitude 125.5 West. Rachel is
moving toward the west-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A turn to the 
northeast is forecast to occur overnight tonight, along with an 
increase in forward speed thereafter. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to 60 mph (95 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Some weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours, 
followed by a steady intensity thereafter until landfall. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 990 mb (29.24 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header
WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
Rachel and the moisture associated with the system will spread over 
portions of the Southwest United States and northern Baja California 
peninsula through this weekend. This will lead to increasing 
coverage of rainfall and for the potential of flash and urban 
flooding.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of
Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and the moisture associated with the system will also bring
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5
inches across the higher terrain, across portions of the Southwest
United States this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of
rainfall and potential for flash and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and 
the Flash Flood Risk graphic at 
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast 
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the 
weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions as well as minor to moderate coastal 
flooding.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
WIND: The risk of tropical-storm-force winds is increasing for 
portions of northern Baja California through extreme northwestern 
Mexico this weekend, and a Tropical Storm Watch may be required for 
a portion of that area later tonight. Strong gusty winds associated 
with the system are expected to spread over interior portions of the 
Southwest United States, especially in areas of higher terrain, from 
this weekend into early next week.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 48
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 090245
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  48
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Thu Oct 08 2026

Rachel's deep convection is barely hanging on. While satellite 
imagery over the last few hours has shown some re-invigoration over 
the northeastern quadrant, Rachel has been primarily defined by weak 
and broken bands surrounding its inner core. The latest subjective 
Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB gave Rachel a 2.5/3.5, 
reflecting a weakening trend, and objective estimates from UW-CIMSS 
continue to trend downward. ASCAT data from around 1830 UTC also 
revealed max winds at around 43 kt. Given these data, Rachel's 
initial intensity has been lowered to 50 kt. 

Initial motion was estimated at around 295/5 kt. Rachel's forward 
speed is expected to slow considerably as it is forecast to be 
picked up by a cutoff low descending from just off the coast of 
California. This will initiate its anticipated northeastward turn, 
followed by an increase in forward speed thereafter. What is 
complicating Rachel's track forecast is the interaction of a much 
broader trough that is forecast to dig down and envelop the western 
US over the weekend. Guidance seems to favor giving Rachel a more 
northerly component in its motion as it approaches northern Baja 
California as a result. The latest NHC track forecast has been 
adjusted once again to fall in line closer to HCCA and GDMI 
guidance, which now favors a leftward shift in the track as Rachel 
approaches land compared to the previous advisory.

The environment surrounding Rachel continues to be characterized by 
dry mid-level air. Thus Rachel's convection is expected to keep 
dissipating, before interaction with the aforementioned low 
potentially reintroduces convection in the form of added instability 
aloft. This will come with the consequence of added vertical wind 
shear, however, which should result in Rachel's vortex further 
degrading. The latest NHC intensity forecast depicts further 
weakening through the next 24 hours, before leveling off thereafter 
to compensate for another potential burst of convection. Rachel, 
however, is still anticipated to become post-tropical either right 
around or shortly after landfall. It should be noted, however, that 
even as a post-tropical cyclone, Rachel is still capable of gusty 
winds and heavy rain along its path. 

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of northern Baja 
California, Mexico, and the northern Gulf of California at tropical 
storm strength over the weekend, and a Tropical Storm Watch could be 
required for a portion of this area later tonight or tomorrow.

2. Strong gusty winds associated with the remnants of Rachel are 
expected to spread over interior portions of the Southwest United 
States, especially in areas of higher terrain, from this weekend 
into early next week.

3. Rachel and the moisture associated with the system will spread 
over portions of the Southwest United States and northern Baja 
California peninsula through this weekend. This will lead to 
increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for flash and urban 
flooding.

4. Swells partly generated by Rachel will continue to build along 
the coast of Southern California and northern Baja California.  
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions, as well as minor to moderate coastal flooding, 
through early next week.  Please consult products from your local 
weather office.

 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  09/0300Z 22.6N 125.5W   50 KT  60 MPH
 12H  09/1200Z 22.7N 125.3W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  10/0000Z 23.4N 124.0W   40 KT  45 MPH

$$

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 7a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 090551
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 7A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
1200 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...SIMON SLOWING DOWN AND MOVING NORTHWESTWARD...
...EXPECTED TO BECOME A DANGEROUS MAJOR HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.8N 104.5W
ABOUT 220 MI...355 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 325 MI...525 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...75 MPH...120 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...985 MB...29.09 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 15.8 North, longitude 104.5 West. Simon is moving
toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h).  A turn to the
north is forecast by early Saturday.  On the forecast track, the 
core of Simon is expected to approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico on Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 75 mph (120 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Rapid intensification is forecast, and Simon is expected to 
become a very dangerous category 4 hurricane before it
reaches the coast of Mexico.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90
miles (150 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 985 mb (29.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area
Saturday afternoon or evening, with tropical storm conditions
expected Saturday morning. Tropical storm conditions are possible
within the Tropical Storm Watch area beginning later today.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 15
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 25 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima
and Jalisco through Sunday.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge is possible along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Thu Oct 08 2026 
864 
WTPZ45 KNHC 090321 CCA
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number   7...Corrected
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 PM CST Thu Oct 08 2026

Corrected malformed non-unicode character in third paragraph.

Simon has become a hurricane this evening.  The satellite
presentation consists of a developing small, intense, central dense
overcast with -82C cold cloud tops, and a primary curved band
wrapping into the center from the northwest part of the cyclone. The
TAFB Dvorak satellite intensity estimate is 65 kt, as well as the
initial intensity for this advisory.
 
Simon's wind radii were adjusted based on a 1920 UTC OSCAT-3
overpass.
 
All conducive ocean heat content, dynamic, and thermodynamic
environmental contributions indicate that Simon should quickly
intensify during the next 24-36 hrs.  Subsequently, the SHIPS RI
index shows a near 70 percent that the cyclone intensity will
increase by 30 kt in 24 hrs.  This seems quite reasonable given that
Simon's inner core is rather small, indicative of a recent AMSR3 MI
pass.  Accordingly, the official intensity forecast will continue to
predict an RI event on Friday, with Simon becoming a category 4
hurricane while heading toward the coast of west-central Mexico.
The NHC intensity forecast is similar to the previous one, is close
to the HFIP-HCCA, and now shows a peak intensity of 120 kt on
Saturday morning.
 
Simon's initial motion is estimated to be west-northwestward, or
295/5 kt.  A turn to the northwest is expected by early Friday. A
northward motion is forecast by early Saturday while high pressure
over central Mexico weakens and shifts eastward, in response to an
amplifying mid-tropospheric trough approaching Baja California. The
HiRes global models that have been to the left of the forecast track
outliers have trended eastward during the past 24 hours, and now
align more with the skilled HCCA and GDMI aids.  Therefore,
confidence in the forecast track is increasing.  The official
forecast is slightly to the left of the previous advisory and a
little slower to conform to the HCCA model, which includes the
Google DeepMind TC ensemble mean.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico
as a major hurricane on Saturday.
 
2. Life-threatening wind and storm surge impacts are expected along
a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a Hurricane
Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita.
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed by
late Friday.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
